# `connection.draw_to_ip`

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask docs-gen` from crates/ew-commands/schemas/connection.draw_to_ip.schema.json. Do not edit: change the source and regenerate. -->

`connection.draw_to_ip` (`DrawToIp`, doc 06 §4.4 "P", WP-S2.04 §5.1, §9.2): a wire that ends in a new
interruption point, in one transaction and one undo step.

- First the IP function and its representation exactly as `ip.place` creates them (`ip` holds `ip.place`'s
  members; the page is the wire's, `external` is absent): `Function {device: none, def, role: main, kind: ip
  {name, direction, star_source, sort}}` and `Representation {functions: [f], page, symbol, pos, orient,
  rep_type: multi_line}`; `def` is `ip.fndef` or the copy the symbol's `fndef` resolves to (must be embedded),
  and its FnDef must have exactly one connection point, which the symbol must draw.
- Then the connection from `a` to that connection point exactly as `connection.draw` creates it: `a` is a CP, a
  junction or a point on an existing connection (which splits it and makes a junction there); the connection is
  `{a, b: the IP's CP, page, route, kind}` with its number unassigned; `route`, when given, is on the page's
  connection grid and meets both CPs exactly (`geometry::require_route`), so it ends at the IP's CP.

Nothing derived is read inside the transaction (the name and the direction are the tool's). Rejected: as
`ip.place` (a missing page or symbol copy, a FnDef that is not embedded, `ip.pos` off the grid) and as
`connection.draw` (a missing endpoint record, off-grid geometry, a route that does not meet its CPs); an IP
symbol whose FnDef has not exactly one CP, or that does not draw it. Interactive. Outcome: the connection.

## Types

### CmdPt2

A point or a displacement [x, y] in nanometres, y downwards (doc 05 §3.2).

Type: array of (integer (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991), integer (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991)) (at least 2 item(s), at most 2 item(s))

### CmdUuid

A lower-case hyphenated UUID naming a record (doc 05 §3.2).

Type: string (at least 36 character(s), at most 36 character(s))

Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$`

### ConnectionKind

The kind of a connection (doc 08 §2.3). `Fluid(FluidLine)` (doc 11) and `SingleLine` (1.0) are additive
variants of their work packages; until then a file's value is kept as `ConnectionKind::Unknown`, which
joins no net (doc 05 §10.3 rule 3).

One of the following forms:

1. **Form 1**: One conductor (the default).

   Shape: `"wire"`

2. **Form 2**: A cable core or shield.

   Shape: object { `core`: [`Uuid`](#uuid) }

   | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `core` | [`Uuid`](#uuid) | yes |  | A lower-case hyphenated UUID (doc 05 §3.2). |

3. **Form 3**: A terminal bridge; joins potentials, never a wire.

   Shape: object { `bridge`: [`BridgeSpec`](#bridgespec) }

   | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `bridge` | [`BridgeSpec`](#bridgespec) | yes |  | A terminal bridge (doc 08 §2.3): the connections of one group are one bridge object. |

4. **Form 4**: A single-line bus connection between bus-port CPs.

   Shape: object { `bus`: [`BusLine`](#busline) }

   | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `bus` | [`BusLine`](#busline) | yes |  | A bus line and the cable that carries it (FR-CBL-008). |

5. **Form 5**: Excluded from nets.

   Shape: `"overview"`

6. **Form 6**: A link between CPs of two functions of one part that no FnDef declares.

   Shape: `"internal"`

| `kind` | [`BridgeKind`](#bridgekind) | yes |  | Bridge kind. |
| `shaft` | integer (format `uint8`, min 0, max 255) | yes |  | The shaft. |

### EndpointParam

An endpoint named in command parameters: a function CP, a junction, or a point on an existing
connection (which splits it and creates a junction there, doc 06 §3.5).

JSON: `{"cp": {"function": "…", "idx": 1}}`, `{"junction": {"junction": "…"}}`,
`{"on_connection": {"connection": "…", "at": [x, y]}}`.

One of the following forms:

1. **Form 1**: Connection point `idx` of a function.

   Shape: object { `cp`: object { `function`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid), `idx`: integer (format `uint16`, min 0, max 65535) } }

   | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `cp` | object { `function`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid), `idx`: integer (format `uint16`, min 0, max 65535) } | yes |  |  |

2. **Form 2**: A junction.

   Shape: object { `junction`: object { `junction`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) } }

   | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `junction` | object { `junction`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) } | yes |  |  |

3. **Form 3**: A point on an existing connection's route.

   Shape: object { `on_connection`: object { `at`: [`CmdPt2`](#cmdpt2), `connection`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) } }

   | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `on_connection` | object { `at`: [`CmdPt2`](#cmdpt2), `connection`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) } | yes |  |  |

### IpAtEnd

The interruption point that `DrawToIp` creates at the end of its wire: `ip.place`'s members without `page`
(the wire's) and `external` (an external connection point is placed with `ip.place`).

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `direction` | [`IpDirection`](#ipdirection) | yes |  | Signal direction. |
| `fndef` | [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) or `null` | no |  | The FnDef copy; default the symbol's. |
| `name` | [`CmdIdent`](#cmdident) | yes |  | The pairing name ("24VDC-2"). |
| `orient` | [`CmdOrient2`](#cmdorient2) | no |  | The orientation. |
| `pos` | [`CmdPt2`](#cmdpt2) | yes |  | The insertion point. |
| `sort` | integer (format `int32`) or `null` | no |  | Chain order. |
| `star_source` | boolean | no |  | The star source of its name. |
| `symbol` | [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) | yes |  | The IP symbol copy. |

### CmdIdent

An identifier: non-empty, one line, NFC, without leading or trailing white space (doc 05 §3.2).

Type: string (at least 1 character(s))

Pattern: `^[^\u0000-\u0020\u007F-\u00A0\u1680\u2000-\u200A\u2028\u2029\u202F\u205F\u3000](?:[^\u0000-\u001F\u007F-\u009F]*[^\u0000-\u0020\u007F-\u00A0\u1680\u2000-\u200A\u2028\u2029\u202F\u205F\u3000])?$`

### CmdOrient2

Orientation: rotation clockwise on the sheet, optionally mirrored (doc 05 §3.2).

Type: one of `"r0"`, `"r90"`, `"r180"`, `"r270"`, `"m0"`, `"m90"`, `"m180"`, `"m270"`

## Exit codes

A command runs as one line of a command log replayed by `ew apply` ([doc 17 §3.5](https://github.com/Ironkode787/ElektraWatt/blob/main/docs/design/17-extensibility.md#35-command-logs-ewcmd)). The exit code of `ew apply` is:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | The line committed as one transaction. |
| 1 | A prevent rule or the command's own domain rule refused the line (`Prevented`, `Rejected`); without `--one-step` the lines before it stay committed and are saved, with `--one-step` nothing is saved. |
| 2 | Anything else stops the replay: invalid parameters, a missing record, an unresolvable reference, an open, lock or save error. |

The codes of every subcommand are in [doc 17 §3.2](https://github.com/Ironkode787/ElektraWatt/blob/main/docs/design/17-extensibility.md#32-exit-codes).
